subject: Cloud Computing
title: Managed Databases as PaaS
description: A micro-lesson that makes Managed Databases as PaaS usable.

hook.text: Running a database yourself means backups, patches, scaling, and 3 AM alerts. Or you let someone else do it.

buildup.text: Managed databases — RDS, Cloud SQL, Atlas — handle the grunt work. You just query your data.

discovery.text: Automatic backups, failover, and scaling mean your database is more reliable than one you'd manage.

twist.text: Managed databases are a form of PaaS. You don't manage the server, just the schema and queries.

climax.text: For most teams, managed beats self-hosted. The cost premium buys sleep and fewer incidents.

punchline.text: Managed databases cost more. They also let you sleep at night.

quiz.question: Why is a managed database considered a form of PaaS?
options: The provider manages the server and infrastructure, you manage the data
You must manage the operating system and networking yourself
Managed databases can only store platform configuration data

details.summary: Managed database services handle provisioning, patching, backups, and scaling of databases so teams focus on queries and schema design. Services like Amazon RDS, Azure SQL, and Cloud SQL support popular engines including PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQL Server.
details.whyItMatters: Database administration is complex and error-prone. Managed databases eliminate operational toil while providing better reliability, automated backups, and built-in high availability.
takeaways: Providers handle patching, backups, and failover automatically
Support popular engines like PostgreSQL and MySQL
Built-in replication and high availability reduce downtime

faq.question: Are managed databases slower than self-managed?
faq.answer: Performance is comparable for most workloads. Managed services offer the same database engines with provider-optimized storage layers. For extreme performance tuning, self-managed databases offer more configuration access, but most applications perform equally well on managed services.

faq.question: What does managed mean for databases?
faq.answer: The provider handles hardware provisioning, OS patching, database engine updates, automated backups, point-in-time recovery, read replicas, and multi-AZ failover. You manage the database schema, queries, users, and application-level performance tuning.
